Rashi on Shabbat 147b:10:1.english: The wine of Perugita - [Perugita is] the name of a country whose wine is excellent.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:10:2.hebrew: קפחו עשרת השבטים - שהיו בעלי הנאה ועסוקים בכך, ולא היו עוסקים בתורה, ויצאו לתרבות רעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:10:2.english: [They] deprived the ten tribes - For they were pleasure-seekers and occupied with this, and were not occupied with Torah, and went out to evil ways.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:11:2.english: He was drawn after them - After the wine and the bathing.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:11:3.english: His learning was uprooted - His learning was uprooted and he forgot it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:1.hebrew: הוי גולה למקום תורה - אם ת"ח אתה, אל תשב אלא במקום ת"ח חברך, ואל תאמר: תלמידים הם, יבואו אלי ודי לי בכך, למה אהיה גולה:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:1.english: Exile yourself to a place of Torah - If you are a Torah scholar, do not reside except in a place of Torah scholars, your colleagues; and do not say, "There are students — they will come to me, and that is enough for me; why should I go into exile?"

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:2.hebrew: שחביריך יקיימוה בידך - שתהא רגיל אצלם, וכשתשנה מסכת אחת והם אחרת, תשמענה ותהא סדורה בפיך, ואל תשתכח הימנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:2.english: As your colleagues will establish it in your hands - That you should be regularly with them, and when you study one tractate and they [study] another, you will hear it and it will be fluent in your mouth, and you will not forget it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:3.hebrew: ואל בינתך אל תשען - לומר, חכם גדול אני וזכרן, וכשאחזור פרק זה או מסכת זו, לא תשתכח חברתה ממני:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:12:3.english: And do not rely on your understanding - [That is,] to say, "I am a great sage and [have a] good memory, and when I review this chapter or this tractate, its companion [chapter or tractate] will not be forgotten by me."

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:13:1.english: A scraper - [In Old French:] estrille [a strigil], and a person scrapes with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:14:1.hebrew: משום פיקא - טיט של אותו נהר מחליק, ובגדי האדם נישורין במים כשהוא נופל, ואתי לידי סחיטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:14:1.english: Because of pika - The mud of that river is slippery, and a person's clothes become soaked in the water when he falls, and he comes to wringing [them out].

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:1.hebrew: אלא בסם - דדמי לרפואה, וגזירה משום שחיקת סמנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:1.english: Only with a drug - For it resembles healing, and [it is] a decree on account of grinding drugs.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:2.hebrew: אבל ביד - להכניס יד לתוך גרונו עד שיקיא, מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:2.english: However, by hand - to insert a hand into his throat until he vomits is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:3.hebrew: מפני הפסד אוכלין - שבמעיו, ומתוך כך הוא רעב וחוזר ואוכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:15:3.english: Because of loss of food - That [is] in his stomach, and as a result he becomes hungry and eats again.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:16:1.hebrew: לפופי - אונמלוטי"א, כמו שעושי' לקטן שיתיישבו אבריו ולא יתעקם:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:16:1.english: Swaddling - [In Old French, enmailloter,] as is done to a young child so that his limbs settle [properly] and he does not become crooked.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:16:2.hebrew: בחומרי שדרה - חוליות של שדרה שנתפרקה אחת מהן, ולאחר זמן קמיירי, דאי ביום לידה אמרי' (לעיל שבת דף קכט:) כל האמור בפ' תוכחה דיחזקאל עושין לחיה בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:16:2.english: With the vertebrae of the spine - [This refers to] vertebrae of the spine, one of which has become dislocated; and [the mishna] is speaking of [a time] later on, for if [it were] on the day of birth, we say (above, Shabbat 129b) [that] everything stated in the passage of rebuke in Ezekiel may be done for a woman in childbirth on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:1:1.hebrew: דלהשתטף - שופכן על גופו, דלאו דרך רחיצה היא, שרי לכתחילה אפי' בחמין:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:1:1.english: To rinse - [This means] pouring them [i.e., water] onto his body; since it is not the [normal] manner of bathing, it is permitted ab initio, even with hot [water].

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:2:1.english: The latter clause - [Refers to:] "But ten people, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:3:1.english: And leaves it in the window - That is adjacent to the wall of the bathhouse.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:4:1.hebrew: הא רבי והא ר"ש כו' - הרי כל אלו שמתירין:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:4:1.english: There is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and there is Rabbi Shimon, etc. - Behold, all of these permit [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:5:1.hebrew: מחצר לגג כו' - ר"ש לטעמיה, דאמר בעירובין (דף עד.): אחד גגות, אחד חצירות, וא' קרפיפות — כולן רשות אחת הן לטלטל מזה לזה, ואפילו של בעלים הרבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:5:1.english: From the courtyard to the roof, etc. - Rabbi Shimon [follows] his [own] reasoning, as he said in Eruvin (74a): Whether roofs, whether courtyards, or whether enclosures — they are all one domain to carry from one to another, even [when they belong] to many owners.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:5:2.english: Until we reached, etc. - And presumably they would not leave it [the towel] by the spring in an ownerless place.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:6:1.hebrew: כבן חכינאי מתני לה - דברי בן חכינאי מסיים בה, ולאו סתמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:6:1.english: He teaches it in accordance with ben Chachinai - He concludes it [with] "the words of ben Chachinai," and [it is] not an unattributed [mishnah].

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:2.hebrew: מביאין בלרי נשים - סדינים שהנשים מסתפגין בהם, מותר להביאן דרך מלבוש לבית המרחץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:2.english: They may bring women's balarei - [These are] sheets with which women dry themselves; it is permitted to bring them in the manner of a garment to the bathhouse.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:3.english: Sikhnita - A large scarf that hangs on him between his shoulders, and his head is wrapped in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:4.hebrew: צריך לקשור שני ראשיה - זה בזה, שלא תפול מראשו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:4.english: One must tie its two ends - [Tie them] to one another, so that it will not fall from his head.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:5.hebrew: כי מעבריתו מאני לבני חילא - כשתביאו בגדי העובדי כוכבי', בני החיל המוטלי' עליכם לשמשן, ואתם מביאים להם בשבת דרך רשות הרבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:5.english: When you transport clothing for the soldiers - When you bring the garments of the idolaters — the soldiers who are imposed upon you to serve them — and you bring [them] to them on Shabbat via the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:6.hebrew: שרביבו בהו למטה מכתפיים - שלא יהיו שוליהם מונחים בכתפיהם, אלא משוכי' למטה, שיהא נראה לבוש:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:7:6.english: Extend them beneath [the] shoulders - [Meaning] that their hems should not be resting on their shoulders, rather drawn downward, so that it appears [like] a garment [being worn].

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:8:1.hebrew: סך ואח"כ ממשמש - [דקסבר] בחול ממשמש ואחר כך סך:
Rashi on Shabbat 147b:8:1.english: One smears oil and afterward rubs - For he holds [that] during the week, one rubs and afterward smears oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:9:1.english: Deyomsit - [The] name of a river whose waters are salty.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:9:3.english: And heals - For the mud is salty.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:9:4.english: All its days - The days of its healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:9:5.english: On this side, etc. - [Is it] from the beginning of the days or at the end?

Rashi on Shabbat 147b:9:7.english: From Passover to Shavuot - Thus, Shavuot is at the end.

Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:16:1.hebrew: אין מעצבין את הקטן - פירשנו [בריש כל הכלים] (דף קכ"ג.) ד"ה אסובי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:16:1.english: "One may not align [the bones of] a young [infant]" - We have [already] explained [this at the beginning of Kol HaKelim] (123a), s.v. Asuvei.

Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:1:1.hebrew: דתניא א"ר כשהיינו למדין תורה כו' - מסתמא יחידי היה, שלא היה אלא אחד מתלמידיו עמו כשהיה רוחץ, כדתניא במקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נא.): שלא ירחוץ תלמיד עם רבו, ואם היה רבו צריך לו — מותר. ומסתמא ר"ש לא היה צריך אלא לאחד כשהיה רוחץ. וכשהיו שבים לביתם היה התלמיד נושא האלונטית בפני עצמה, שר"ש לא היה נושא עמו, דהא ס"ל שיחיד מותר להביאה ולא חיישינן לסחיטה. והא דקאמר "היינו" — ר"ל כל אחד ואחד בפני עצמו, כשהיה מגיע יומו לשמש רבו. ולעיל בפ' כירה (שבת דף מ:) גרסינן: מעשה בתלמיד של ר' מאיר שנכנס אחריו לבית המרחץ; ויש ספרים דגרסי "תלמידיו", ואיננו; ובכל הספרים גרסי לקמן בפרק שואל (שבת דף קנא:) "תלמידו". מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:1:1.english: As it was taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said, "When we were studying Torah, etc." - Presumably he was alone, for only one of his students was with him when he would bathe, as it is taught in [the chapter] Makom SheNahagu (Pesachim 51a): A student should not bathe with his teacher, and if his teacher needs him, it is permitted. And presumably R. Shimon only needed one [student] when he would bathe. And when they would return to their home, the student would carry the towel on his own, for R. Shimon would not carry [it] with him, since [R. Shimon] holds that an individual is permitted to bring it and we are not concerned about wringing [it out]. And that which [Rabbi] says "we were" — he means to say each one individually, when his day arrived to serve his teacher. And earlier in the chapter Keirah (Shabbat 40b) we have the reading: "An incident with a student of R. Meir who entered after him into the bathhouse"; and there are texts that read "his students," which is incorrect; and in all the texts they read later in the chapter Sho'el (Shabbat 151b) "his student." [From my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:7:1.hebrew: צריך לקשר שני ראשיה למטה - בגיטין בפ' הנזקין (גיטין דף נט.) מפרש דסכניתא הוא בגד דק, דאמרינן: "סוכני וחומר כי אמגוזא ופלגא דאמגוזא". ומשום הכי צריך לקשר שני ראשיה למטה, שלא יפריחנו מעליו הרוח ואתי לאתויי; או משום דנראה כעין משוי, לפי שהוא דק מאד ואינו נראה מלבוש אא"כ נראה קשור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147b:7:1.english: One must tie its two ends below - In Gittin, in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 59a), [the Gemara] explains that a sikhnita is a thin garment, as we say [there]: "Sukhni and chomer [are] like a nut and half a nut [in size]." And for this reason one must tie its two ends below, so that the wind will not blow it off him and he will come to carry [it]; or because it looks like a type of burden, since it is very thin and does not look like a garment unless it appears tied.
